lesson_title: Springs, Sprinklers and a Closing Ledger: Physics Exam Essentials
hook_text: Your phone pulls the Earth EXACTLY as hard as the Earth pulls your phone. Same force. So why does only the phone hit the floor?
clip_script: Newton's third law loses its spookiness the moment you see every force as a two-ended spring. A spring never pushes at one end only — compress it and BOTH ends push outward; stretch it and both ends pull inward. Every force in nature is such a spring between two objects: the Earth pulls the dropped phone and the phone pulls the Earth, with exactly equal force. The phone does all the visible moving because it is absurdly lighter — same spring, wildly different masses hanging on its two ends.
visual_style: A glowing spring stretched between a falling phone and the entire planet; two force arrows of identical length at the spring's ends; the phone streaking down while the Earth nudges by less than an atom's width, proved with an absurd zoom-in.
mood: Mind-flip wonder — the law everyone recites and almost nobody believes, made obvious.
pacing: Slow reveal of the spring, the equal-arrows beat held for effect, then the punchline of the Earth's imperceptible budge.
call_to_action: Watch the full revision lesson and take five audit habits into the examination room.
